registered_corridor.parameters: Set g=lambda=chi=hbar=1, r=-N^4 and c=N^-4 for an integer N>=2 in the exact positive-lambda full-oscillator Q3LOCK model.
registered_corridor.phase_quantities: The inherited collective well scale and infrared strength become theta_Q=N^4/6 and A0=8 c theta_Q^2=2N^4/9. Since I3<51/100, A0>I3 for every N>=2.
registered_corridor.thermal_threshold: Let rho_N=sqrt(I3/A0)=3 sqrt(I3/2)/N^2 and beta_star_N=3 I3 atanh(rho_N)/rho_N. The function atanh(rho)/rho is increasing on (0,1), so beta_star_N decreases in N. Moreover rho_N^2<=9(51/100)/32 and atanh(rho)/rho<=1/(1-rho^2), whence beta_star_N<4896/2741<9/5. Thus every N>=2 and beta>=9/5 lies strictly in the inherited EXP-000782 sufficient phase regime.
registered_corridor.finite_beta_conclusion: For every N>=2 and beta>=9/5, the exact full-oscillator fixed-lattice model has a strict zero-source pressure cusp and at least two distinct parity-related tempered Euclidean DLR tangent states with opposite collective magnetizations. EXP-000781 supplies their locally normal time-zero restrictions and local Gibbs/DLR energy tightness; EXP-000790 supplies separate phasewise abstract OS/KMS reconstructions, not one common pre-existing alpha.
registered_corridor.order_density: For x_(beta,N)>0 solving x tanh(x)=3 beta/(2N^4), delta_(beta,N)=N^4[tanh(x)/(6x)-I3/(2beta)]>0. The endpoint pressure slopes are at least sqrt(delta_(beta,N))/8 in absolute value and the DLR magnetizations are at least plus/minus sqrt(delta_(beta,N)).
registered_corridor.ground_quantities: The inherited half-Watson constant J3 obeys J3^2<=I3<51/100. Therefore rho_star_N=N^4/6-J3 N^2/(2 sqrt(2))=N^2[N^2/6-J3/(2sqrt(2))]>0 for every N>=2.
registered_corridor.ground_conclusion: Along the inherited beta-first dyadic ground sequence, liminf <S_L^2>/V^2>=rho_star_N, the full finite-volume gap obeys Delta_L^full<=1/(2 V m_L^2) and limsup V Delta_L^full<=1/(2 rho_star_N), and the ground-energy density has e_N(h)-e_N(0)<=-|h|sqrt(rho_star_N)/8. Source differentiation plus local energy compactness gives two distinct parity-related locally normal time-zero tangent candidates with Q_0 expectation at least plus/minus sqrt(rho_star_N).
registered_corridor.novelty_boundary: The parent EXP-000782/789/790 theorems are unchanged. The new result is the exact simultaneous specialization to the registered large-N model corridor, including one N-independent beta threshold and explicit N-dependent ground-order constants. It bypasses Ritz cutoff passage but does not identify the DFFR Ritz branches with the full-oscillator DLR branches.

l1_first_duhamel_reduction.setup: Let h>=0 have compact resolvent, let B>=0 commute with h, and let V=B^(1/2) C B^(1/2) for a contraction C. Put F_B(t)=Tr(B exp(-t h)). For beta>0 define K_beta(s)=exp[-(beta-s)h] V exp(-s h), 0<s<beta.
l1_first_duhamel_reduction.ritz_passage: If g_beta belongs to L1(0,beta) and Pi_M are increasing spectral projections commuting with h, then Pi_M K_beta(s) Pi_M converges to K_beta(s) in trace norm for every s, is dominated by g_beta, and converges in L1((0,beta);S1). Hence the first Duhamel coefficient integral passes through the spectral Ritz limit in trace norm.
l1_first_duhamel_reduction.boundary: This is a conditional first-coefficient reduction. It is neither a DFFR transition-norm estimate nor a contour expansion, and it supplies no Q3 short-time integrable majorant.

short_time_obstruction.fixture: On l2(N_{>=1}), let h e_n=n e_n and V=B=h. Then for every t>0 the one-time dressed operator exp(-t h/2)V exp(-t h/2) is trace class with norm F_B(t)=sum_(n>=1)n exp(-tn)=exp(-t)/(1-exp(-t))^2.
short_time_obstruction.failure: F_B(t) is asymptotic to t^-2 as t decreases to zero and is not locally L1. Thus pointwise positive-time trace class does not automatically supply the short-time L1 domination used by the conditional reduction.
short_time_obstruction.firewall: For this commuting fixture the actual fixed-beta cross integrand K_beta(s)=h exp(-beta h) is constant in s and trace class. The fixture does not refute existence of the first Duhamel coefficient, DFFR entry, or a different transition-resolved/time-integrated estimate. It strictly sharpens the earlier moving-dimension fixed-time boundary only at the level of automatic one-time L1 domination.
